The default export is the initialized client or `undefined` in an unconfigured production build, so later instrumentation can safely use `posthog?.capture(...)`. Updated `src/main.tsx` to import this module before React mounts, ensuring browser initialization happens once. Set both real public configuration values in `.env.local` through `set_env_values`. `.env.example` already listed the two required Vite keys with non-production values, so it was intentionally left unchanged.
handoff.forNextAgent: Import the default client from `src/lib/posthog`; do not call `posthog.init` elsewhere. Since production may intentionally have no configuration, use optional chaining for client calls. There is no CSP in the inspected project, so `script-src`, `connect-src`, and `worker-src` were all left untouched. Do not run build/lint/tests as part of this completed initialization step.
handoff.evidence: Read the final `src/lib/posthog.ts` and bootstrap import, and `check_env_keys` confirmed `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` and `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST` are present in `.env.local`. `package.json` already declares `posthog-js`; no dependency change was needed.

handoff.goals: Wire client-side PostHog identification so authenticated users receive a stable distinct ID, person properties are set safely, and identity resets on logout.
handoff.did: Updated `src/pages/Admin.tsx` at the existing Supabase authentication boundary. The Admin screen now identifies an existing session and each `SIGNED_IN` session with the stable Supabase `user.id`. It sends optional email and admin role only as PostHog person properties, never in event properties. A tracked active ID resets PostHog before a direct account switch, while `SIGNED_OUT` resets PostHog and clears the tracked identity. This ensures subsequent browser events and SDK-reported errors inherit the authenticated browser identity without re-identifying at individual event callsites.
handoff.forNextAgent: Import and use the initialized default client from `src/lib/posthog` with optional chaining for browser instrumentation. No caller needs to add a distinct ID to normal browser events or error reporting: the Admin auth lifecycle persists it after successful authentication and clears it on logout. This is a client-only Vite app; no server-side PostHog integration was identified.
handoff.evidence: Read the final `src/pages/Admin.tsx` after editing and confirmed it imports the initialized PostHog client, identifies with `authenticatedUser.id` for the initial session and `SIGNED_IN`, conditionally attaches email/role as person properties, and calls reset on `SIGNED_OUT` or a changed authenticated ID. Per task instructions, no build, lint, or tests were run.
handoff.assumptions: Supabase `User.id` is the application's immutable canonical user identifier, and Supabase emits `SIGNED_IN`/`SIGNED_OUT` through its existing auth-state subscription.

handoff.goals: Configure one global PostHog mechanism so browser errors the React application does not catch reach Error Tracking.
handoff.did: Updated `src/lib/posthog.ts`, the existing browser-only PostHog singleton initialization, with an explicit `capture_exceptions` configuration. It captures uncaught window errors and unhandled promise rejections as PostHog exception events while keeping console-error capture disabled. This feeds PostHog Error Tracking with app-level unhandled exceptions without adding manual capture calls across components or routes.
handoff.forNextAgent: The global error mechanism is configured at the existing PostHog initialization point; do not initialize PostHog again or add per-component exception wrappers for this requirement. Production builds remain safely unconfigured when the environment values are absent, as established by the prior init step. Source maps, build verification, and any project-level Error Tracking settings are outside this instrumentation-only task.
handoff.evidence: Read the final `src/lib/posthog.ts` after the edit and confirmed `capture_exceptions` enables `capture_unhandled_errors` and `capture_unhandled_rejections`, with `capture_console_errors: false`. Confirmed the installed posthog-js SDK exposes exception-autocapture configuration. Per task constraints, no build, lint, tests, dependency installation, or app startup was run.
handoff.assumptions: This Vite/React browser entry initializes the singleton before mounting, as documented in the prior task handoff. PostHog project-side Error Tracking exception autocapture is enabled or will be enabled for the project, consistent with the supplied web reference.

Admin event calls use the persisted identity established by the prior identify task and include only controlled action/published metadata where relevant.

Public visitor actions are intentionally plain/personless browser captures; authenticated Admin events inherit the stable Supabase user identity established at the existing auth lifecycle. No server-side instrumentation was added because this is a client-only Vite app. The review task should validate TypeScript/build behavior; per task instructions, no build, lint, or tests were run.
handoff.evidence: Read each modified source file immediately before editing, then reread the completed capture sites and event manifest. Confirmed all 11 manifest names match their capture calls, captures occur only after successful operations or on the actual CTA click, every call uses `posthog?.capture`, and event properties are controlled non-PII values only.

handoff.reportSection:
## Starter analytics dashboard

Created [Analytics basics (wizard)](https://us.posthog.com/project/627104/dashboard/2132614) with five wizard-tagged views: lead request volume, WhatsApp lead requests, shipping quote conversion, admin publishing activity, and admin publishing activation. The views cover the exact planned event contract and will populate as production events arrive.

handoff.goals: Configure PostHog log capture for this project's supported runtime using the documented JavaScript web SDK-native logging path, while exporting only purpose-written lines added in this run.
handoff.did: Updated `src/lib/posthog.ts` to enable the posthog-js native Logs stream with the stable service identity `nodavexa-web` and Vite deployment mode. Created `src/lib/posthog-logs.ts` as the dedicated PostHog logger wrapper. It emits only five structured, privacy-safe outcome records added by this run: contact submission completed/failed and shipping quote calculated/unavailable/lookup failed. Updated `src/pages/Contact.tsx` and `src/components/QuoteCalculator.tsx` to call that wrapper at their existing completed/error outcomes. No existing console output or existing application logger is exported; console capture was deliberately not enabled. Log attributes contain only controlled workflow/outcome values and quote quantity, never request bodies, postal codes, solution names, contact-form content, or other user data.
handoff.forNextAgent: No package installation is required for review: the existing `posthog-js` dependency is version `^1.434.12`, which exceeds the documented Logs minimum of 1.368.0. No new environment variables were added; log delivery reuses `VITE_POSTHOG_KEY` and `VITE_POSTHOG_HOST` configured by upstream. To verify delivery, submit the public contact form or calculate a shipping quote with a valid postal code, then open https://us.posthog.com/logs and filter by service `nodavexa-web`; delivery remains unverified until a record is observed. Only lines added in this run are exported. If the user later explicitly wants browser console/application output routed to this exporter, add `captureConsoleLogs: true` inside the existing `logs` init configuration after auditing that output for secrets and PII.
handoff.evidence: Read the JavaScript web commandment file, installed and read the `logs-javascript` skill and its JavaScript reference, confirmed the project is browser-only Vite with no existing client logging configuration, and reread all modified files after changes. Confirmed `captureConsoleLogs` is absent and all new logging calls flow through the dedicated wrapper. Builds, lint, dependency manifest changes, and lockfile updates were intentionally left to review per task instructions.
handoff.assumptions: The configured browser PostHog endpoint accepts Logs for the supplied project and the Vite `MODE` value accurately describes each deployment environment.
